description: SustDataED2 provides 96 days of aggregate and individual appliance electricity measurements from one Portuguese household. Its OSF metadata specifies current and voltage waveforms at 12.8 kHz, eighteen appliance readings at 0.5 Hz and timestamps for appliance on and off transitions. Building-energy modellers can use these traces to test load disaggregation, occupancy-linked demand or demand-response logic before applying a model to larger housing stocks. A single monitored home does not represent national household behaviour, and the high-rate signals require careful time alignment. The public OSF node opened and its file-provider list was visible; the DOI registration states CC BY 4.0. I did not download recordings or verify each individual file. The descriptor links separate monitoring and disaggregation code, reviewed as distinct G1 items. The traces support residential electricity-demand simulation when their single-home scope is respected.
